subject: GriffinTech evaluation: criteria, tests, and next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@griffintech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: GriffinTech call — goals, priority criteria, and candidate tests

Hi Alyssa / Elliot — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed test plan so we stay aligned heading into the bake-off.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary business driver: improve user experience for your support assistant where latency spikes and inconsistent results are causing poor CSAT.
- Key technical pain: headroom during peak batches, token-cost variability on long-context transcripts, and lack of deterministic KV cache across model variants.
- Compliance ask: PHI touches in transcripts; Griffin needs isolated tenancy or private deployment and clear audit logs.

Decision criteria (what you said mattered most)
1) Latency: 95th percentile for short-turn requests < 200ms, and long-context (2k token) throughput with tail latency < 800ms.
2) Cost profile: predictable unit costs for sustained 1M-token/month workloads (target threshold saved in eval matrix).
3) Reliability/fallback: seamless fallback to a smaller quantized model with no >1% degradation in top-1 correctness for the priority prompts.
4) Security & governance: SOC 2, configurable retention, KMS/HSM key management, and region-bound hosting.

Competitive context you mentioned: Vertex managed endpoints and InferaLabs (self-hosted managed service). We will design tests to surface the KV cache and dropout behaviors you flagged.

Proposed bake-off tests (we can adjust)
- Test A: Short-turn latency (50–200 token prompts) — 1k concurrent steady-state for 30m.
- Test B: Long-context throughput (2k tokens, mixed batching) — 500 concurrent sustained for 60m.
- Test C: Cache effectiveness — scripted prefix reuse to measure real-world cost delta and cache hit rates.
- Test D: Failover & rollout — simulate node failure during load to validate fallback policy and correctness.

Deliverables we will share before the smoke test
- Eval matrix (attached: griffin_eval_matrix_v1.xlsx) with scoring rubric and thresholds.
- Mutual action plan (attached) with target dates and owners.
- A short smoke-test playbook we will run on Jan 22 (draft attached).

Next steps
1) You confirm the decision criteria and add any procurement/security blockers (Elliot / procurement team).
2) We schedule a 45m smoke test week of Jan 20–26 (aiming for Jan 22).
3) Redwood prepares a tailored quantized model, reserved pool config, and a short sample dataset for correctness checks.

Alyssa — happy to loop your procurement contact if you prefer procurement in the next reply.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@griffintech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Chan <elliot.chan@griffintech.com>, GriffinTech Procurement <procure@griffintech.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GriffinTech call — goals, priority criteria, and candidate tests

Thanks Camila — this is helpful, and the matrix looks like the right place to capture thresholds. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirm PHI requirement: we need either a private VPC deployment in us-west or an on-prem option for the live dataset runs.
- Security gating: SOC 2 type II is required for pilot (we'll share our security checklist).
- Procurement: we generally need an MSA + SOW; will the mutual action plan translate into a draft SOW for the pilot?

Evaluation extension (things we want measured explicitly)
- Cost delta per 1M tokens with and without prefix caching enabled.
- Model quality: top-3 match rate on our 200 prompt gold set (we'll share the set once NDA/LOU is in place).
- Auditability: can you expose request/response traces and K/V cache hits with customer-controlled retention?

We're okay to target Jan 22 for the smoke test — please put a proposed time slot (we are PST-based). I will loop procurement and Elliot will add the security questionnaire.

Cheers,
Alyssa Morgan
Director of Product, AI Platforms
Alyssa.Morgan@griffintech.com | (646) 555-0123

[Attachment: griffin_security_questions_v1.docx (docx)]

  * Draft SOW for pilot and timeline mapping to MAP (Camila / Marissa).

- Proposed timeline
  * Jan 22 — smoke test: short-turn latency + cache verification (30–45m).
  * Jan 29 — full throughput run and failover test (2 hours).
  * Feb 5 — decision readout with Griffin stakeholders.

- Test owner notes: Karthik, please confirm expected infra (reserved pool size, GPU type, networking). I will prepare the quantized snapshot and baseline metrics by Jan 21.
